candidates.extract: Grays railway station is on the London, Tilbury and Southend line, serving the town of Grays, in Essex, England. It lies 19 mi down the line from , via ; it is located at the junction where a branch line from via rejoins the route from Rainham.

candidates.name: Tilbury Town railway station
candidates.extract: Tilbury Town railway station is on a loop line of the London, Tilbury and Southend line, serving the town of Tilbury, Essex (also known as Tilbury Town). It is 21 mi down the line from London Fenchurch Street via and it is situated between and .

Port of Tilbury
candidates.description: Port on the River Thames at Tilbury in Essex, England
candidates.extract: The Port of Tilbury is a port located on the River Thames at Tilbury in Essex, England. It serves as the principal port for London, as well as being the main United Kingdom port for handling the importation of paper.

candidates.name: TS Queen Mary
candidates.extract: TS Queen Mary is a Clyde steamer launched in 1933 at the William Denny shipyard, Dumbarton, for Williamson-Buchanan Steamers. The ship is currently moored at Glasgow Science Centre, in Glasgow, where she is being restored to active service.

candidates.name: Tilbury
candidates.extract: Tilbury (or Tilbury Town) is a port town on the north bank of the Thames in the borough of Thurrock in Essex, England. The town was established as separate settlement near East and West Tilbury and Tilbury Fort in the late 19th century, on land that was mainly part of the parish of Chadwell St Mary.

Bata shoe factory
candidates.extract: The Bata shoe factory in East Tilbury is what remains of an industrial estate in Essex, England, which produced shoes for over 70 years. Founded in 1932 by Tomáš Baťa, the factory was "one of the most important planned landscapes in the East of England" in the 20th century.

candidates.name: West Tilbury
candidates.extract: West Tilbury is a village in the borough of Thurrock in Essex, England. It stands on a 30 m high ridge of land overlooking the River Thames.

candidates.name: Gravesend–Tilbury Ferry
candidates.extract: The Gravesend–Tilbury Ferry was a passenger ferry across the River Thames east of London. It was the last public crossing point before the Thames reached the sea.

candidates.name: Linford Wood
candidates.extract: Linford Wood is a 3.5 ha Local Nature Reserve in Linford in Thurrock, Essex. It is owned and managed by Thurrock Council.

candidates.name: Kings Head, West Tilbury
candidates.extract: The Kings Head Pub is a grade II listed pub in the conservation area of West Tilbury, in the Thurrock district, in the ceremonial county of Essex, England. The pub closed in 2015 and in May 2016 Punch Taverns sold the pub, as part of their corporate strategy, to housing developers.

candidates.name: Bill Meroy Creek
candidates.extract: Bill Meroy Creek is a small waterway flowing into the Thames to the east of Tilbury Fort in West Tilbury which from 1851 marked the eastern boundary of the area in which duty had to be paid on coal entering London.
